subject: Private deployment throughput runway & surge budget — architectural probe
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: HorizonAI Ops <ops@horizonai.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Private deployment throughput runway & surge budget — architectural probe

Hi Sandy / Horizon ops team,

Thanks again for the deep dive earlier — this thread captures the sizing assumptions and a short list of questions we need answered before we lock the canary scope. Attached is a baseline spreadsheet (horizon_privpool_throughput_matrix_v1.xlsx) with the model mix we discussed and preliminary token/QPS targets. High level:

- Target 1 (initial canary): sustained 1200 concurrent requests at median 40 tokens/request (approx 48k tokens/min) targeting p95 < 180ms for short-chat flows and p99 < 600ms for longer-gen requests.
- Target 2 (post-canary ramp): sustained 3k concurrent with burst headroom to 6k for 10 minute windows.
- Planned initial dedicated pool: equivalent of 6 A100-class GPUs, autoscale to 18 in 3 stages (policy described in sheet).

Key constraints we need from you to validate network/runway:
1) Confirm on-prem egress cap from the Horizon datacenter (we have 25 Gbps listed, please confirm sustained and burst allowances).
2) Expected % of gen traffic that is long-context (>= 4k tokens) vs short-chat (<= 512 tokens) over the first 60 days.
3) Maintenance windows / preferred canary dates and any blackout periods.

Operational asks from Redwood:
- We'll propose a canary window of 2 weeks with staged traffic ramps and a fallback to hosted models for any SLA breaches.
- We plan to ship a canary runbook (canary-run-plan.md) and a lightweight observability dashboard to your SRE team prior to go-live.

Attachments: horizon_privpool_throughput_matrix_v1.xlsx (workbook), canary-run-plan.md (markdown runbook).

Next steps: please reply with the egress confirmation and traffic split by 2028-08-31 so we can finalize the provisioning request. If agreeable, I'll schedule a 60-minute canary kickoff with your SREs next week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Principal Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment throughput runway & surge budget — architectural probe

Marissa / Sandy — quick technical notes from the runtime side to align expectations. Quoting Marissa below.

On Tue, Aug 28, 2028 at 9:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> [snip] Target 1 (initial canary): sustained 1200 concurrent requests ...

Notes:
- Model mix: if >=30% of requests are long-context (>4k), we need to change the kernel selection and KV cache policy; that reduces effective throughput per GPU by roughly 35% in our benchmarks. Please call that out in the traffic split.
- Network: MTU/segment sizes matter for our token streaming. If your top-of-rack switches do <9k MTU, we recommend path MTU discovery validation.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache warmup will be critical for p95 latency. Plan for a 45–60 minute warm-up stage with synthetic replays before the canary starts.
- Storage: prefer local NVMe for model artifacts on the serving nodes; fallback to NFS will add ~10–20ms variance per request under high concurrency.

I've attached a short ops checklist we use for on-prem canaries. If Horizon prefers, we can run a stress test from Redwood's staging fleet to emulate the burst window prior to provisioning.

- Jonas
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment throughput runway & surge budget — architectural probe

Marissa / Jonas — thanks for the clear summary and the checklist. A few data points from our side: 

- Confirmed network: our datacenter has a 25 Gbps aggregated egress limit per cluster. We can open a temporary burst window to 40 Gbps for a 2-hour test with advance notice, but sustained at 25 Gbps is the operational cap.
- Traffic split (expected first 60 days): ~65% short-chat (<=512 tokens), ~25% medium (512–2048 tokens), ~10% long (>=2048 tokens). Well provide a log sample by EOD Friday.
- Maintenance windows: weekly SAT 02:00–04:00 local (UTC-7) is preferred blackout; avoid GOV holiday next month (Sept 5).
- Canary: procurement can provision the initial hardware in 4 business days after mutual sign-off. We can commit to a 2-week canary starting as early as 2028-09-11 if provisioning is approved by 2028-09-05.

Request: please provide a canary traffic ramp schedule (by day), rollback criteria (latency / error thresholds) and a list of Redwood contacts for the 24/7 on-call during canary. Also confirm whether Redwood will handle the model artifact transfers and initial cache seeding.

Sandy Park
Head of Infrastructure
HorizonAI
sandy.park@horizonai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 02 Sep 2028 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment throughput runway & surge budget — architectural probe

Thanks Sandy — that aligns well with our assumptions. Summary of decisions and next steps (action items):

Decisions
- Canary window: 2028-09-11 to 2028-09-25 (2 weeks).
- Initial committed pool: 6x A100-equivalent serving nodes (local NVMe), autoscale policy to 12 after day 4 if p95 and error budgets are healthy, to 18 by day 10 if traffic ramps as expected.
- Network constraints: design for sustained 25 Gbps. We'll plan synthetic 2-hour burst tests at 40 Gbps during the canary with 48-hour notice.
- Cache warmup: Redwood will handle cache seeding and initial artifact transfer; plan a 1-hour synthetic replay before opening traffic.

Action items (owners / deadlines)
- Horizon: confirm the log sample and final traffic split by 2028-09-03 (Sandy).
- Redwood: share canary ramp schedule & rollback criteria by 2028-09-04 (Marissa / Jonas). See: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1A2b3HorizonPrivPool for the draft canary-run-plan.
- Procurement/Provisioning: Horizon will provision hardware by 2028-09-05 if sign-off complete (Sandy).
- On-call rota: Redwood to provide 24/7 contact list and escalation ladder by 2028-09-06 (Jonas).

Canary ramp (proposed)
- Day 0–1: 10% baseline traffic replay + warm-up
- Day 2–4: 25% steady-state traffic, verify p95 & error < 0.5%
- Day 5–7: 50% steady-state, introduce 10m burst windows to 75%
- Day 8–11: 75% steady-state, run 2-hour 40Gbps synthetic burst test
- Day 12–14: 100% target steady-state (move to autoscale to 18 if traffic requires)

Rollback criteria (examples)
- p95 latency exceeds target by >30% for >10 minutes
- error rate >1% sustained over 5 minutes
- repeated OOMs or node loss >2 in a 1-hour window

Links & attachments: horizon_privpool_throughput_matrix_v1.xlsx; canary-run-plan.md (draft updated). HubSpot: HS-94281.

I'll kick off the canary kickoff invite once Horizon confirms the log sample and provisioning window. Appreciate the quick turn here — will keep communication tight.

Best,
